baseline_fields.evidence_summary: PCEF now has bounded immutable checkpoint replay/fork semantics validated across fresh processes. Historical application state can be reopened and forked without rewriting the original branch. Consequential replay is blocked until the source mission is sealed at verified TERMINAL; the child binds both the historical checkpoint receipt and the source terminal receipt. Replay effect identities are unique across the checkpoint thread, later source effects are synchronized into the replay deny set, sibling-fork reuse is rejected, failed reservations remain blocked, fork authority cannot escalate, fork-root identity and ancestry are verified, and forged historical receipt/state metadata is rejected even when the local checkpoint hash is recomputed. Source and fork child each complete the canonical eight-receipt PCEF lifecycle. External-provider replay, distributed checkpoint storage/reservation, native-device binding and production replay adoption remain unproven.
baseline_fields.single_extra_feature: Sovereign Proof-Carrying Autonomy: historical state may replay or fork only when its proof lineage, authority and effect identity remain sealed and independently verifiable.
baseline_fields.8x8_parity_gate: Adopt checkpoint replay/fork through the canonical PCEFCheckpointReplayV1 surface in real production workflows, then prove distributed/native/external-provider replay without weakening sealed-source, receipt-membership or lineage-wide exactly-once constraints.

frontier_patch.definition: Every consequential agent/tool/external effect must carry authorization-bound, idempotent, replay-verifiable proof before terminal completion; risky execution must prove isolation; guarded runs must prove session/guardrail/trace completeness; historical replay must preserve immutable branch history, prove source/checkpoint receipt lineage and forbid historical effect identity reuse.
